q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of an induction cooktop?
title: Induction cooktop carbon footprint per unit
short: Add the glass top, copper coil, circuit board, fan and plastic body per cooktop with supplier figures. Add assembly and testing electricity, divide the unit's energy by cooktops passed, and report by power rating.

ul: Copper induction coil and ferrite bars.
Control board, fan and plastic housing.
Load and safety testing, then packing.

p: Report per cooktop with its wattage. The board and glass top usually carry most of the bought-in footprint.

example.title: Worked example: induction cooktop unit per unit (one month)
lines: Plant total: 10,650 / 30,000 = 0.355 kg CO2 per unit
Add glass, coil, board and housing for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
